If its owner is present, he need not repay it. But if he hired it, he must pay its hire.
If someone seduces a virgin and sleeps with her, he must marry her, and she shall become his wife.
But if [?] refuses to give her to him in marriage, he must give her father her bride-price, the bride-price paid for a virgin.
Do not let a sorcerer live.
Anyone who has sexual intercourse with an animal shall be sentenced to death.
Whoever sacrifices to gods, rather than to the Lord alone, shall be destroyed.
Do not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, because you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Do not mistreat any widows or orphans.
If you mistreat them and they cry out and call to me, I will certainly hear their cry.
I will become furious in my anger and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows, and your children orphans.
If you lend money to a poor person among your people, do not oppress him or charge him interest.
If your neighbor gives you his garment as a pledge, return it to him before the sun sets.
For it is his only covering and the garment that covers his nakedness; he has nothing else to sleep in. If he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.
Do not revile the gods, and do not speak evil of the ruler of your people.
Do not delay the [?] of your threshing floor or the produce of your threshing floor. You shall give me your firstborn son.
You shall do the same for me with your cattle, your sheep, and your donkeys. The young animal shall remain with its mother for seven days, and on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
You shall be holy people to me. Do not eat the flesh of an animal killed by a wild beast; throw it to the dogs.
Do not spread a false report, and do not join with someone who acts unjustly, lest you become an unjust witness.
Do not join the majority in doing wrong, and do not side with the majority to pervert justice.
Do not favor a poor person in judgment.
If you find your enemy’s ox or his donkey, take it back and return it to him.
If you see your enemy’s donkey overwhelmed by its load, do not pass by, but help him with it.
Do not pervert justice for a poor person, and do not act unjustly in judgment.
Keep away from every unjust judgment. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous, and do not spare the guilty.
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds their eyes and distorts a just statement.
Do not oppress foreigners, for you know how foreigners feel, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
For seven years sow your fields and gather your harvest.
But in every seventh year leave it to rest, so that the poor of your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what remains. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.
You shall do all your work for six days, but on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your slave woman and the foreigner may be refreshed.
Observe everything I have said. Do not mention the names of gods, and do not speak them with your mouths.
Three occasions for your festivals.

Keep the feast at the time prescribed by the law. For seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, in the new months, for that was when you came out of Egypt. Do not appear before me empty-handed.

Celebrate the Feast of Harvest with the first produce of your labor from what you sowed in your fields, and the feast at the end of the year, when you gather the produce of your labor from your fields.
Three times every male shall appear before me, the Lord your God.
Do not offer the blood of my sacrifices with leaven, and do not let the fat of my feast remain overnight until the next morning.
Bring the first fruits of your fields into the house of the Lord your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I am sending my angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you into the land that I have prepared for you.
Be on your guard and listen to him. Do not disobey him, for he will not forgive you; my name is upon him.
If you listen to my voice and keep everything I tell you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
My angel will go, guiding you, and bring you among the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Destroy them.
Do not bow down to their gods or worship them, and do not follow their practices. You must completely overthrow them and smash their pillars to pieces.
Worship the Lord your Creator. I will bless your bread, your wine, and your water, and I will remove sickness from among you.
No one in your land will fail to bear children, and no one will be barren. I will give you the full number of your days.
I will send fear upon anyone who resists you, and I will terrify all the nations whose lands you enter. I will deliver all your enemies to you, so that they flee from you.
I will send ahead of you something that terrifies them and drives out the Amorites, Hittites, Hivites, and Canaanites.
I will not drive them out in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild animals of the land do not multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you become numerous and inherit the land.

I will establish your boundaries from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the great river Euphrates. I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hands and drive them out before you.
Do not make an agreement with them or obey their gods.
They must not live in your land, so that they do not cause you to sin. If you worship their gods, they will become a snare to you.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy elders of the people of Israel, and let them bow down to the Lord from a distance.”
Moses alone is to approach the Lord. The others must not approach, and the people must not go up with them.
Moses came and told the people all the Lord’s words and his judgments. All the people answered with one voice, saying, “We will do everything the Lord has spoken, and we will obey.”
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Moses rose early in the morning and built an altar beside the mountain, and twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed cattle as peace offerings to the Lord.
Moses took half the blood and poured it into bowls, and he poured the other half of the blood onto the altar.
Moses took the book of the covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, “We will do everything the Lord has spoken, and we will obey.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, saying, “Here is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”
Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy leaders of Israel went up.
They saw the place where the God of Israel stood. Beneath his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, like the appearance of the expanse of heaven when it is clear.
And the chosen men of Israel, who had no equals, appeared in the place of God, and they ate and drank.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you stone tablets bearing the law and the commandment that I have written, so that you may instruct them.”
And Moses and Joshua rose and went up the mountain of God.
And Moses said to the elders, “Do not stir until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. If anyone comes with a legal dispute, let him go to them.”
And Moses went up the mountain, and a cloud hid the mountain.
The splendor of the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
And the appearance of the Lord’s work was like a blazing fire flaring on the summit of the mountain before the Israelites.
And Moses entered the midst of the cloud and went up the mountain, and he stayed thirty days and thirty nights.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell the Israelites: ‘Take an offering for me from your possessions, as you have resolved in your hearts.’ Accept the offering.
And this is the offering you are to receive from them: gold and silver;
bronze, blue cloth, purple cloth, spun scarlet yarn, twisted fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, skins dyed blue, and wood that does not decay;
sardius stones and stones to be engraved for the ephod and the robe.
And you shall make a sanctuary for me, and I will appear among you.
And you shall make for me everything that I show you on the mountain: the pattern of the tent and the pattern of all the tent’s furnishings. You shall make them accordingly.
And you shall make for me an ark of the testimony from wood that does not decay, two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
And you shall cover it with pure gold inside and outside. You shall cover it and make a gold molding [?] around it.
And you shall cast four gold rings for it and place them at its four supports: two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
And you shall make its carrying poles from wood that does not decay and cover them with gold.
Insert its poles into those four rings on the supports of the ark, as carrying poles for the ark by which they will carry it.
In the rings, as I commanded you, let the poles be fitted so that they do not move.
And you shall put into the ark the commandment that I am going to give you.
Make a covering of pure gold to fit above it, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
And you shall make two cherubim from sheets of pure gold and place both of them at the ends of the cover.
One cherub shall be made at this end, and one cherub at the other end of the cover. You shall make the two cherubim at its two ends.

The cherubim shall spread their wings upward, sheltering the cover with their wings, and their faces shall look toward one another over the cover. Make them this way, with the faces of the cherubim looking toward one another.
Place the covering on top of the ark, and put inside the ark the commandment that I will give you.

And I will make myself known to you there, and I will speak to you from above the cover, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, giving you every commandment that I command for the Israelites.
And you shall make for me a table of pure gold, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
Make a wavy gold molding around it, and make its rim four fingerbreadths wide.
Make clasps for the molding on its rim.
Make four gold rings and place them at the four corners by its legs, toward its rim.
Its [?] shall serve as sockets for its carrying poles, with which the table is lifted.
Make its carrying poles from wood that does not rot, and overlay them with pure gold. The table shall be carried with them.
Make its dishes, its bowls, its pouring vessels, and its measuring vessels with which you will pour. Make them of pure gold.
Place bread on the table before me continually.
Make a lampstand of pure gold. Make the lampstand of hammered work, its shaft and its branches. Its cups, knobs, and flowers shall be made as one piece with it.
Six branches shall be made on its sides: three branches of the lampstand on one side and three branches on the other side.
Its three cups shall be joined with one flowering knob. It shall be the same for all six branches that come out of the lampstand.
For the shaft of the lampstand, make four cups, with its flowers and its rounded tops.
Its knob shall be between the two branches. It shall be the same for all six branches that come out of the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be one piece with it, all hammered from a single piece of pure gold.
Make its seven lamps and arrange the lamps so that they give light toward one side.
Fashion what is behind it and its arrangement [?] from pure gold.
See that you make everything according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
For the tabernacle, make ten curtains of twisted fine linen, blue, purple, and twisted scarlet yarn. Make them with cherubim, the work of a skilled weaver.
The length of each curtain shall be eighty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits. Each shall have the same measurements.
Five curtains shall be joined, one joined to another, and five curtains shall be linked to one another.
Make blue loops for them along the edge of the curtain, on the outer side, at the second joining.
Make fifty loops for the first curtain, and make fifty loops along one edge of the curtain at the end of the second set. Their edges shall face one another.
Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is one whole.
Make a sackcloth covering over the tabernacle. Make eleven sackcloth curtains.
Each sackcloth curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. These shall be the measurements of each one.
Join five sackcloth curtains together, and join seven sackcloth curtains together separately. Fold the sixth sackcloth curtain over at the front of the tabernacle.
Make fifty loops along the edge of one curtain, at the middle where the curtains are joined. Make fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain, where it is joined to the first.
Make fifty bronze clasps, put the clasps into the loops, and join the sackcloth curtains so that they form one whole.
Lay the excess portion of the sackcloth over the tabernacle. Use what remains as a covering; the excess from the tabernacle’s sackcloth curtains shall cover the back of the tabernacle.
A cubit of the excess sackcloth curtains of the tabernacle shall cover the sides of the tabernacle, on one side and on the other.
Make a covering for the tabernacle from dyed sheepskins, and a covering of blue leather above it.
Make the tabernacle’s posts from wood that does not rot.
Each upright shall be ten cubits high and one and a half cubits wide.
Two supporting tenons for each frame, so that one frame is joined to another. Do the same for all the frames of the tabernacle.
Make twenty frames for the north side of the tabernacle.
Make forty silver sockets for the twenty uprights: two sockets for one upright, for its two faces, and two sockets for another upright, for its two faces.
And twenty frames for the other side, the south side.
Their bases, which support the frames, shall be forty silver bases, two bases for each frame, one on either side.
For the back of the tabernacle, on the side toward the sea, make seven frames.
And two additional frames for the corners at the back of the tabernacle.
They shall be aligned at the bottom and joined evenly at the top of the frame into one joint. Do the same for both corners; they shall be aligned.
There shall be eight frames and seventeen silver bases, two bases for each frame, two bases for each frame on all its sides.
Make crossbars of wood that does not decay, five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle.
And five crossbars for the supports of the tabernacle on its other side, and five crossbars for the rear frames among the supports of the tabernacle on the side toward the sea.
The crossbar in the middle of the frames shall pass through, joining one support to the other.
Its frames shall be overlaid with gold, and the openings through which its crossbars pass shall be overlaid with gold.
Build the tabernacle according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
Make for it a curtain of blue, purple, double-dyed scarlet, and finely twisted linen. Make it with a weaver’s workmanship, and make cherubim on it.
Set it on four pillars of wood that does not decay, overlaid with gold. Within its pillars there shall also be gold, and their capitals shall be gold, and their four bases shall be silver.
Place the curtain on the pillars, and bring the ark of the testimony there, inside the curtain. The curtain shall separate the inside from the outside of the sanctuary.
The curtain shall conceal the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Set the table before the curtain, on its outer side, within the tabernacle, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side. Place the table on the north side of the tabernacle.
Make for it an entrance curtain of blue, purple, double-dyed scarlet, and doubled fine linen, worked in varied embroidery.
Make five pillars for the curtain and overlay them with gold. Their capitals shall also be gold, and cast five bronze bases for them.
Make an altar of wood that does not decay, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
Make the altar, and make horns for it at its four corners. Its horns shall project from it, and overlay it with bronze.
Make for it pans for the sacrifices, its shovels, its bowls, its meat forks, and its fire pans. Make them all of bronze.
Make its grating of bronze, openworked like a fishing net. Make four bronze rings for the grating at its four corners.
Place them below, in the altar’s grating, and the grating shall extend halfway up the altar.
Make carrying poles of wood that does not decay for the altar, and overlay them with bronze.
Insert the carrying poles into the rings, so that they are on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Its boards shall be hollow. Make it that way, just as I showed you on the mountain; make it that way.
Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the side facing southwest, make hangings for the courtyard from twisted fine linen, a hundred cubits long along that side.
Its pillars shall be twenty, and its bronze bases twenty; its hooks and bands shall be silver.

Likewise, on the side facing north, the hangings shall be a hundred cubits long. Its pillars shall be twenty, and its bronze bases twenty. Its hooks and bands for the pillars and their bases shall be overlaid with silver.
Across the width of the courtyard facing the sea, the hangings shall measure fifty cubits. Their pillars shall be ten, and their bases ten.
The width of the courtyard facing east shall be fifty cubits. Their pillars shall be ten, and their bases ten.
The hangings on one side shall be twenty-five cubits long. Their pillars shall be three, and their bases three.
On the other side, the curtain shall stand fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.

For the entrance to the courtyard, there shall be a curtain twenty cubits long, made of blue, purple, scarlet, and twisted fine linen, decorated with needlework. Its pillars shall be four, and its bases four.
All the pillars around the courtyard shall be overlaid with silver bands. Their tops shall also be silver, and their bases bronze.
The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and five cubits high, made of twisted fine linen, with bronze bases.
All its workmanship, all its equipment, and the stakes of its courtyard shall be bronze.
Command the Israelites to bring pure, beaten olive oil from the first pressing for the light, so that they may keep a lamp burning inside the tabernacle, in the sanctuary.

Outside the curtain, before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it burning before the Lord from evening until morning. This shall be a perpetual ordinance for your generations among the Israelites.
Bring near to you your brother Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, so that they may serve me as priests: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Make holy garments for Aaron, for honor and splendor.
Inform all those skilled in heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom. They shall make holy garments for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve me in holiness.

These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a full-length robe, a patterned tunic, a man's [?] for the waist, and a sash. Make holy garments for Aaron and his sons, in which they shall serve me as priests.
They shall take for me gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
They shall make his ephod from twisted fine linen, skillfully woven with decorative work.
It shall have two shoulder pieces joined to one another, one upon the other, worked on its two sides.
The woven bands of their ephod, above them, shall be joined to them as part of the same workmanship, made of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen.
Take two emerald stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.
Six names shall be on one stone and six on the other stone, according to their families.
With the work of a skilled craftsman, engrave both stones with the names of the sons of Israel, as a seal is engraved.
Place the two stones on its two shoulder pieces as a memorial for the Israelites. Aaron shall carry their names before the Lord on his two shoulders as a memorial for them.
And you shall make wild animals of the earth from pure gold.
Make two borders of pure gold, joined with floral work. Make braided work, and place the border of the braid upon the wild animals of the earth [?], according to their form, at the front.
You shall make a breastpiece of judgment, with varied woven work, according to the design of the ephod. You shall make it likewise of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen.
You shall make it square and doubled, a cubit long and a cubit wide.
And it shall be set with settings, with its stones in four rows. A row of stones shall be made of sardius, topaz, and emerald: one row.
The second row shall have a coal-like stone, a sapphire, and a jasper.
The third row shall have a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
The fourth row shall have a gold-colored stone, a beryl, and an onyx. Each row shall be mounted in gold and secured with gold.

Its stones shall be made according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names. They shall be engraved like the face of a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes of Israel.
You shall make braided borders for the breastpiece, and braid them like a cord of pure gold.
Aaron shall carry the names of the children of Israel on his back, at the place from which the word of judgment comes forth, when he enters the sanctuary, as a memorial before the Lord.
And you shall place it opposite where the hooks of its chain project [judgment], on both sides, from its shoulder pieces; and you shall place it from the judgment [?].
You shall place images of animals on the front of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod.

You shall place the command and uprightness toward the judgment-piece [?], and it shall be put on Aaron’s back. When he enters the sanctuary before the Lord, Aaron shall carry the judgment of the children of Israel on his back before the Lord continually.
You shall make a full-length robe entirely of blue.
The opening of the robe shall be made from the robe itself and shall be in the middle. Woven work shall be made around the opening of the robe, with its seam on the inside, so that it does not tear.

And above it and below it you shall make things like pomegranate fruit, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, below the woven garment, all around it. Join it [?] to golden pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
And the golden pomegranates, their bells, and their flowers shall be at the [?] of his garment all around.
Aaron shall wear it when he offers sacrifice, with a sound that can be heard as he enters the sanctuary before the Lord, and likewise as he goes out, so that he does not die.
You shall make a thin gold plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, like a seal, ‘Holy to the Lord.’
And you shall put it on a blue thread, and they shall place it on the serpent, so that it rests at the end of the serpent.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead. Aaron shall bear the people’s sin concerning the holy things that the children of Israel consecrate among all their holy gifts. It shall be on Aaron’s forehead for acceptance before the Lord.
The fastening [?] of his tunic shall be of fine linen. You shall make a turban of fine linen and a sash worked in various colors.
For Aaron’s sons you shall make garments, sashes, and turbans. They shall be for honor and splendor.
You shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with him. Anoint them, cleanse their hands, and bless them, so that they may offer sacrifices to me.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their nakedness. They shall cover them from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter the tent of testimony and when they enter to offer sacrifice at the altar of the sanctuary. They shall not bring sin upon themselves, so that they do not die. This is a perpetual statute for him and his descendants after him.
This is what you shall do for them to consecrate them to serve me: take a bull from the cattle and two unblemished rams.
Also take unleavened bread mixed with oil and unleavened wafers with oil. You shall make them from fine wheat flour.
You shall place it in a basket, and you shall also place the bull and the two rams in a basket.
You shall bring Aaron and his two sons to the entrance of the tent of testimony and wash them with water.
Take his garments and clothe Aaron your brother with his full-length robe, and his garment shall extend to the turban.
Put the turban on his head and place the gold plate on his turban.
Take some of the blessed oil and pour it on his head.
Bring his sons forward too, and dress them in their garments.
Fasten their sashes around them and put their head coverings on them. Their priestly service to me shall be everlasting. Ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of testimony. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the bull's head before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Slaughter the bull before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out all the remaining blood beside the altar.
Take all the fat of its entrails, its liver, its two kidneys, and its kidney fat, and place them on the altar.
Take the bull's flesh, hide, and dung outside the camp and burn them, for it is a sin offering.
Take one ram. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram's head.
Slaughter that ram, take its blood, and pour it onto the altar, sprinkling it all around.
And you shall cut it into its separate pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and place its head among the pieces you have cut.
And you shall offer the whole ram on the altar as an offering to the Lord.
Take another ram. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter it and take some of its blood. Put it on the tip of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. Put it also on the tips of the right ears of Aaron's sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet.

Take some of the blood of the sacrifice and some of the blessed oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and his garments, and afterward on his sons and their garments. He and his clothing, and his sons and their clothing with them, shall be made holy. Pour the ram's blood onto the altar all around.
Take the fat from that ram. Take the fat covering its entrails, its liver, its two kidneys, and its kidney fat. Take its right foreleg, for ordination is performed by this.
And take one loaf made with oil and a wafer from the basket in which all the unleavened bread is placed before the Lord.
Place all of it in Aaron's hands and in the hands of Aaron's sons, and set it apart as an offering before the Lord.
And you shall take it from their hands and offer it on the altar as a pleasing aroma before the Lord. It is an offering to the Lord.
And you shall take the breast of the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and present it as a special offering before the Lord, and it alone shall be your portion.
Consecrate the breast and set it apart. Set apart the shoulder too, as you set apart the rams of ordination from Aaron and his sons.

And it shall be a perpetual ordinance for Aaron and his sons among the Israelites, because this is a special offering. It shall be a special offering from the Israelites, from the sacrifices they offer for their deliverance, a special offering to the Lord.
Aaron's holy garments shall belong to his descendants after him, so that they may be anointed in them and ordained.
The priest from among his sons who succeeds him shall wear them for seven days when he enters the tent of testimony to be appointed in the sanctuary.
And you shall take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the ram's flesh and the bread in the basket at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
They shall eat it where it was consecrated, for their ordination and consecration. An outsider shall not eat it, for it is holy.
If any of the flesh of the ordination sacrifice or any of the bread remains until morning, burn what remains with fire. It shall not be eaten, for it is holy.
Do all this for Aaron and his sons, just as I commanded you, for seven days, to ordain them.
Offer a bull each day for sin, with which you shall cleanse the altar when you consecrate it, and anoint it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it. Your altar shall be most holy, and whatever touches that altar shall become holy.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two unblemished year-old lambs each day, continually, as a regular offering of lambs.
You shall offer one lamb in the morning and one toward evening.
With one lamb, offer a tenth of a hin of fine wheat flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.

The other lamb, which you offer toward evening, you shall offer in the same manner as your morning offering. You shall also make the same drink offering, as a pleasing aroma. It is an offering to the Lord.
It shall be a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the entrance of the tent of testimony, before the Lord. There I will make myself known to you, to speak to you.
There I will give commands to the Israelites, and I will be sanctified by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of testimony and its altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve as priests for me.
I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might be called upon by them and be their God.
You shall make me an altar for incense from wood that does not decay.
Make it square, one cubit long and one cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns shall be made as one piece with it.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold—its base, its sides all around, and its horns—and you shall make a gold molding around it.

You shall make two rings of pure gold for it, at the surrounding edge of its plate. You shall make them on its two sides, on its two flanks. You shall surround it with a rim and provide carrying poles with which to carry it.
You shall make its carrying poles from wood that does not decay and cover them with gold.
You shall place it before the curtain that is over the ark of testimony, where I will make myself known.
Aaron shall burn finely compounded incense on it every morning.
When he tends the lamps each evening, he shall burn incense on it, as a continual incense offering before the Lord throughout their generations.
You shall not put incense of a different composition on it. You shall not pour sacrificial produce or a drink offering upon it.
Once each year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns with blood that cleanses sin. Once each year he shall perform this cleansing throughout their generations. It is most holy to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
When you take a census of the Israelites and count them, each shall give the Lord a ransom for his life, so that no plague comes upon them when they are counted.
This is what everyone who comes to be counted shall give: half a didrachm, according to the sacred didrachm. The sacred didrachm is twenty obols. Half a didrachm shall be an offering to the Lord.
Everyone who comes to be counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall bring their offering to the Lord.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than half a didrachm when they bring their offering to the Lord as a ransom for their lives.

You shall take the silver that the Israelites have brought as their offering and give it for the service of the tent of testimony. It shall be a remembrance for the Israelites before the Lord, as a ransom for their lives.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Place it between the tent of testimony and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it.
When they enter the tent of testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die; likewise when they enter the sanctuary to serve, when they offer a sacrifice to the Lord.
They shall wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. This shall be a permanent law for them and for their descendants after him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Take fragrant spices: five hundred shekels of choice myrrh blossoms, fragrant cinnamon half as much as the first ingredient—two hundred and fifty—and two hundred and fifty of fragrant calamus;
and five hundred of [?], measured by the sanctuary shekel, and olive oil.
Make it into holy anointing oil, a perfume prepared by a perfumer.
With it you shall anoint the tent of testimony and the ark of testimony,
and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its utensils, and the altar,
and the place where they sacrifice and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
You shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Whatever touches them shall become holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them so that they may serve me.
Tell the Israelites: ‘This anointing oil shall be holy among you throughout your generations.
No outsider shall anoint himself with it, and no other perfumer shall make this perfume. You yourselves shall not make anything like it, because this oil is holy and shall be holy to you.
If you make it, and whoever gives some of it to someone of another family, he shall be cut off from his people.’”
The Lord said to Moses, “Take spices for yourself: liquid storax, fragrant onycha, and gleaming frankincense. All shall be prepared in equal amounts.
Let its maker make it into incense, a preparation of fragrant incense. Make it a pure and holy preparation.
Grind some of it finely and place it before the tent of testimony, where I will make myself known to you. This incense shall be most holy to you.
You shall not make an imitation of this incense using this preparation. It shall be set apart for you and holy to the Lord.
Whoever has any of it made in order to enjoy its fragrance shall be destroyed from among his people.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Look, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
“I have filled him with a holy spirit, wisdom, knowledge, and skill in every kind of work, so that he may devise designs
and be a master craftsman, working in gold, silver, and bronze, in blue and purple material, spun scarlet thread, and twisted fine linen,
and in stonework for construction and woodcarving, so that he may carry out every kind of work.”
And I have provided Eliab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. And I have given understanding to everyone skilled in heart, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
The tent of testimony, the sacred ark, the cover over it, and the equipment of the tent;
and the altar, the table and all its equipment, and the pure lampstand and all its equipment;
and the basin and its stand;
and the garments they made for Aaron, and the garments of his sons, in which they will serve me.
And the oil used for anointing and the incense burned for the sanctuary. And they shall make everything I command you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

“You must command the Israelites and tell them, ‘Take care to keep my Sabbath, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who makes you holy.’
And keep my Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Whoever profanes it shall certainly be put to death. Whoever does work on it—that person shall be cut off from their people.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall certainly [?] be put to death.
The Israelites shall keep the Sabbaths, observing them throughout their generations.
It is an everlasting ordinance. It is an everlasting sign between me and the Israelites, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he finished and rested.”
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him two tablets of the commandment, stone tablets written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they rose up against Aaron and said to him, “Get up and make us gods who will go before us, for we do not know what has happened to that man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt.”
Aaron said to them, “Take the gold earrings from the ears of your wives and daughters, and bring them to me.”
And all the people took off the earrings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He received it from their hands, shaped it into an image, and made it into a cast calf. They said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
When Aaron saw it, he built an altar in front of it. Aaron made a proclamation, saying, “Tomorrow is a festival of the Lord.”
Aaron rose early in the morning, offered sacrifices, and brought an offering of peace sacrifices. The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, “Go, hurry down from here, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have sinned.

They have quickly turned away from the path you commanded them to follow. They have made themselves a calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
And now leave me alone, and in my anger and wrath I will destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.
Moses pleaded before his God and said, “Why, Lord, do you rage in anger against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with exalted power and a mighty arm?

Do not let the Egyptians say, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and destroy them from the earth.’ Cool the anger with which you have raged, and be merciful toward your people’s wickedness.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said, ‘I will greatly multiply your descendants, making them as numerous as the stars of heaven. I will give all this to your descendants, and they will possess it forever.’”
The Lord relented concerning the disaster he had said he would bring upon his people.
Moses turned and came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the commandment in his hands, stone tablets written on both sides, written on one side and on the other.
The tablets were the Lord’s work, and their writing was God’s writing, engraved on the [?].
When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “There is the sound of battle in the camp.”
Moses said to him, “This is not the sound of messengers who are gaining strength, nor is it the sound of messengers of war. Rather, what I hear is the sound of the messengers of wine.”
When Moses approached the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Moses became angry, threw the two tablets from his hands, and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, scraped it down and ground it to powder, scattered it into the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What have you done to these people, bringing such a great sin upon them?”
Aaron said to Moses, “Do not be angry, my lord. You yourself know the disposition of these people.
They said to me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us, because we do not know what has happened to that man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt.’
I told them, ‘Whoever among you has gold, bring it.’ They brought it and gave it to me. I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.”
When Moses saw that the people had rebelled, that Aaron had caused them to rebel, and that they had become a laughingstock to their enemies,
Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever has chosen the Lord, come to me!” All the descendants of Levi gathered around him.

And he said to them, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Let each man carry his sword. Go from gate to gate through the camp, and let each man kill his brother, let each man kill his fellow, and let each man kill his neighbor.”
And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them, and three thousand men from among the people fell at that time.
Moses said to them, “Today you have consecrated yourselves to the Lord with your own hands, each at the cost of his son and his brother, so that a blessing may be bestowed upon you.”
And on the next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. And now I will go up to the Lord to obtain forgiveness for your sin.”
Moses returned to the Lord and said, “I beg you, Lord: these people have committed a great sin and have made gods of gold.
Now, if you will forgive them this sin, forgive it. But if not, erase me too from your book in which you have written me.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned before me, I will erase from my book.
Now go and lead these people to the place I told you about. Look, my angel will go before you. On the day when I call them to account, I will bring their sin back upon them.”
And the Lord killed some of the people because they had made the calf that Aaron made for them.

The Lord said to Moses, “Go up from here, you and your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
I will send my angel before you, and he will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Girgashites, and Hivites.
He will bring you into a land flowing with milk and honey. But he will not go up with you, because your people are stubborn, lest he destroy them along the way.”
When the people heard this bad news, they mourned deeply.

The Lord said to the Israelites, “You are a stubborn people. Beware, lest I bring another plague upon you and destroy you. Now take off your splendid clothes and your ornaments, and I will show you what I will do with you.”
The Israelites took off their ornaments and their clothes at Mount Horeb.
Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp. It was called the Tent of Testimony. Anyone who sought the Lord would go to that tent outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went to enter that tent outside the camp, all the people would stand, each watching from the entrance of his own tent. They would watch Moses as he went, until he entered the tent.
After Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and speak to Moses.
All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent (and speaking with Moses), and all the people would stand at the entrances of their tents and bow down.
The Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as someone speaks with his friend. Moses would then return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, who was a young man, would not leave the camp.

Moses said to the Lord, “Look, you tell me, ‘Lead these people,’ but you have not told me whom you will send with me. Yet you yourself said to me, ‘I know you above all others, and you have found favor with me.’

And if indeed I have found favor with you, reveal yourself clearly to me, so that I may know and see you, so that I may find favor before you, and so that I may know that this great nation is your people.
The Lord said to him, “I will go before you and give you rest.”
Moses said, “If you yourself do not go with us, do not bring me up from here.”
How will it be known that I and your people have truly found favor before you unless you go with us? Then I and your people will be honored among all the nations on earth.
The Lord said to Moses, “I will also do this thing you have asked of me, because you have found favor before me, and I know you above all others.”
Moses said to the Lord, “Show me your glory.”

The Lord said to Moses, “I will pass before you in my glory and proclaim the name of the Lord before you. I will have mercy on the one on whom I have had mercy, and show compassion to the one to whom I have shown compassion.”
The Lord said to Moses, “You cannot see my face, because no human being can see my face and live.”
And God said to Moses, “Here is a place beside me, and you shall stand on the rock.”
Until my glory passes, I will place you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will remove my hand, and you will see my back, but my face will not be visible to you.

The Lord said to Moses, “Carve two stone tablets for yourself like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. I will write on those tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.”
“Be ready in the morning, and go up Mount Sinai. Stand there before me on the mountaintop.”
No one is to come up with you, and no one is to be anywhere on the mountain. Neither sheep nor cattle are to graze near that mountain.
Moses carved two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai as the Lord had commanded him, taking the two stone tablets with him.
The Lord came down in a cloud, stood there, and called on the name of the Lord.
And the Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, merciful and compassionate, slow to anger, abundant in mercy, and righteous,

who preserves righteousness and shows mercy to thousands, who forgives wrongdoing, error, and sin, but does not acquit the guilty; who brings the fathers’ sins upon their children and their children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”
Moses hurried, bowed down to the ground, and worshiped the Lord.
And Moses said, “If I have found favor before you, let my Lord go with us, for this people is stubborn. Forgive the sin and guilt of your people, and we will belong to you.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I am making a covenant with you before all your people. I will do great and glorious things that have never been done anywhere on earth or among any nations. All the people among whom you live will see the work of the Lord, because what I will do for you is awe-inspiring.”
But observe everything I command you. Look, I will drive out before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Take care, then, not to make a sworn agreement with the people who remain in the land you are entering, so that they do not become a cause of stumbling for you.
You must tear down their altars, break their images, cut down their sacred groves, and burn the carved images of their gods with fire.
For you must not worship another god, because the Lord God's name is Jealous, and God is jealous.

Beware of making a sworn agreement with those who live in that land. They will prostitute themselves by following their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and they will invite you, and you will eat from their sacrifices.

You will take some of their daughters for your sons and give your daughters to their sons. Your daughters will prostitute themselves by following their gods and cause your sons to prostitute themselves by following their gods.
You must not make gods of cast metal for yourself.

Observe the festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Miyazya, because in the month of Miyazya you came out of the land of Egypt.
Every male that opens the womb is mine—the firstborn of cattle and the firstborn of sheep.
Redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a sheep. If you do not redeem it, give its price. Redeem every firstborn among your children, and do not appear before me empty-handed.
Do your work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. Rest from sowing and rest from harvesting.
“You shall celebrate the Sabbath festival for me when the wheat harvest begins, and the Festival of Booths in the middle of the year.”
Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the God of Israel.
When I drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, no one will desire your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times a year.
Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, and do not let what is sacrificed for the Passover festival remain overnight until morning.
Bring the first produce of your land to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a lamb while it is still suckling its mother's milk.
The Lord said to Moses, "Write these words down for yourself, for according to these words I will establish a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses remained there before the Lord for forty days and forty nights. He ate no food and drank no water, and he wrote these words, the Ten Commandments, on the tablets.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, the two tablets were in his hands. As he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the appearance of his face had become radiant while he spoke with the Lord.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and saw that his face had become radiant, they were afraid to approach him.
Moses called them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation came back to him, and Moses spoke to them.
After this, all the Israelites approached him, and he commanded them to do everything the Lord had told him on Mount Sinai.
When he finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face to conceal it.
Whenever Moses went before the Lord to speak with him, he removed his veil until he came out. When he came out, he told the Israelites everything the Lord had commanded him.
The Israelites saw that Moses' face had become radiant and that he put on a veil to conceal it until he went in to speak with him.
Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, "This is what the Lord has said you must do:
For six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day there shall be a holy rest, a Sabbath of rest for the Lord. Whoever does work on it shall be put to death.
Do not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on my Sabbath days. I am the Lord."
Moses spoke to the whole congregation of the Israelites, saying, "This is what the Lord has commanded:
Take an offering for the Lord from them. Let all whose hearts move them bring from the first of their possessions: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue and purple cloth, double-dyed scarlet cloth, spun linen, and goat hair;
ram skins made into leather, [?] leather, and wood that does not decay;
onyx stones and gemstones for engraving, for the ephod and the robe.
Let everyone among you who is skilled come and make everything the Lord has commanded:
the tabernacle, its enclosure, its covering, its hooks, its bars, and its pillars;
the ark of [?], its carrying poles, and its lid;
And the enclosure of the courtyard and its pillars;
And emerald stones;
And the table and all its utensils;
And the lampstand for lighting and all its utensils;
And the oil used for anointing and the incense burned as incense;
And the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, and the altar and all its utensils;
and the garments of Aaron the priest, and the garments in which they serve in the sanctuary;
And the robes of Aaron’s sons for their priestly service.
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites left Moses’ presence.

They brought offerings, each according to what he had resolved in his heart and willingly desired. They brought an offering to the Lord for all the work on the tent of testimony, for everything needed, and for all the sacred garments.
The men also brought things from the women, everyone as his heart willingly desired. They brought signet rings, earrings, rings, necklaces, bracelets, and every kind of gold ornament.
Everyone brought gold as an offering to the Lord, and everyone who had ram skins dyed red and skins of [?].
Everyone who had pledged an offering of silver or bronze brought an offering to God. Everyone who had wood that does not decay brought it for all the work needed for the tabernacle.
Every skilled woman who could spin with her hands brought spun yarn of blue, purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.
And all the women whose hearts prompted them skillfully spun the goats’ hair.
The leaders also brought emerald stones and gemstones to be set in the robe and in the shoulder-piece, and for the requirements of its service;
And oil for anointing and ingredients for incense.
Every man and woman whose heart willingly moved them to bring offerings and carry out all the work that the Lord had commanded Moses brought them. The Israelites brought an offering to the Lord.
Moses said to the Israelites, “Look, the Lord has called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
He filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge;
So that he might be the master craftsman over everything, carry out every kind of master craftsmanship, and work in gold, silver, and iron;
And practice the craft of working gemstones, work in wood, and carry out every kind of work skillfully.
He also put the ability to teach into his heart and into the heart of Eliab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan.

He filled them with skill so that they would know how to carry out all the work of the sanctuary that required weaving, weaving with scarlet yarn and fine linen, and carrying out every kind of craftsmanship, each in his own work.
Bezalel, Eliab, and all the skilled people who had been given wisdom and complete understanding carried out all the work required for the sanctuary, everything that the Lord had commanded.

Moses called Bezalel, Eliab, and all those who had skill, to whom the Lord had given understanding in their hearts, and everyone whose heart willingly moved them to work, to come to this work and complete it.

They received from Moses the offering that the Israelites had brought for carrying out all the work of the sanctuary. They continued to receive further offerings from those who brought them every morning.
Then all the skilled workers who were carrying out the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing;
And they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more offerings than are needed for the work that God commanded to be done.”
Moses gave an order and proclaimed throughout the camp that neither men nor women should make any more tithe offerings for the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing them.
For they had enough to do the work, and some was left over.
And all the skilled workers who made the sacred garments made them for Aaron the priest, as God had commanded Moses.
They made the ephod of gold, blue cloth, purple cloth, twisted scarlet thread, and fine linen.
They cut the gold leaf and made it into threads to be woven with blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver.
They made the ephod with shoulder pieces extending down over both shoulders, woven with a distinct braided pattern.
They made its waistband as part of it, worked in the same way, of gold, blue cloth, purple cloth, twisted scarlet thread, and fine linen, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They prepared all the emerald stones and surrounded them with gold, engraving them like the engraving of a seal with the names of the children of Israel.
They placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the children of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece with intricate woven work, like the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, blue cloth, purple cloth, twisted scarlet thread, and fine linen.
The breastpiece was square and folded double, a span wide and a span long when doubled.
Four rows of precious stones were worked into it. One row consisted of sardius, topaz, and emerald; this was the first row.
The second row consisted of red jacinth, dark jacinth, and jasper.
The third row consisted of ligure, agate, and amethyst.
The fourth row consisted of a gold-colored precious stone, beryl, and onyx. They were surrounded with gold and secured with gold.

There were twelve precious stones bearing the names of the children of Israel, corresponding to their names. They were engraved like the engraving of a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
They made braided cords for the border of the breastpiece, worked like twisted cords, of pure gold.
And they made two twisted circlets and two gold rings.
They placed the two gold rings at the two ends of the breastpiece.
They attached the braided gold cords to those two rings on the two sides of the breastpiece, with the two braided cords at its two attachment points.
They placed them on the two coiled settings and attached them toward the shoulder pieces of the ephod, facing its front.
They made two gold rings.
They placed them toward the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, underneath on its front, at its joining point, above the woven band of the ephod.

He fastened the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod. They were secured with blue cords and woven into the [?] of the ephod, so that the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as God had commanded Moses.
They made the garment called the under-robe, to go beneath the ephod, entirely woven of blue cloth.
The opening of the under-robe was in its middle, woven with braided edging around the opening, and [?].
At the bottom of the under-robe they made shapes like pomegranate blossoms when they bloom, of blue cloth, purple cloth, twisted scarlet thread, and fine linen.
They made gold bells and placed the bells along the edge of the under-robe, all around it, between the pomegranates.
A gold bell and a pomegranate alternated along the edge of the under-robe, all around it, for them to serve in, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And they made linen tunics, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons;
And a linen turban, a linen headdress, and undergarments of fine linen.
And they made their sashes of fine linen, blue, purple, and twisted scarlet thread, with embroidered work, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And they made the holy plate, set apart for the sanctuary, of pure gold.
And they put an inscription on it, engraving it like a seal: “Holy to the Lord.”
And they attached a blue cord to it so that it would rest above the turban.
And they made ten curtains for that tabernacle.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long, and each curtain was four cubits wide.
And they made the veil of blue, purple, twisted scarlet thread, and finely twisted linen, the work of a weaver, and they worked figures of cherubim into it.
And they placed it on four pillars of wood that does not decay, overlaid with gold. Their capitals were gold, and their four bases were silver.
and they made an embroidered curtain for the doorway of the tabernacle, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver, and depicted cherubim on it.
And its five pillars, their rings, their capitals, and their bands they overlaid with gold; and their five bases were of bronze.
And they made the courtyard on the south side, with hangings of finely twisted linen around the courtyard, one hundred cubits long.
Its pillars were twenty, and their bases were twenty, made of bronze.
And on the north side there were one hundred cubits, with twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases.
And the courtyard on the west side was fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and ten bases.
And the courtyard on the east side was fifty cubits.
And the hanging on the south side was fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
And at the back of the other side, on either side of the entrance to the courtyard, its hangings were fifteen cubits each, with three pillars and three bases.
And all the hangings of the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
And the bases of their pillars were bronze, and the fastenings of their pillars were silver. Their capitals were overlaid with silver, and all the pillars of the courtyard were overlaid with silver.

And the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was embroidered with blue, purple, twisted scarlet thread, and finely twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long, and its width, measured vertically, was five cubits, matching the hangings around the courtyard.
And its four pillars had four bronze bases. Their fastenings were of silver, their capitals were covered with silver, and the pillars themselves were covered with silver.
And all the pegs of the courtyard were bronze.

And this was the arrangement of the tabernacle of the testimony, as Moses had been commanded by the Lord, so that its work would belong to the Levites under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
And Bezalel, the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, made these things as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, was a master craftsman in weaving, needlework, and embroidery, weaving with scarlet thread and fine linen.
And Bezalel made the ark.
And he overlaid it with pure gold, outside and inside, and made a gold molding around it.
And he cast four gold rings for its four corners, two on one side and two on the other side.
Handles by which they grasp it when they lift it.
And he made the atonement cover above the ark of pure gold.
And he made two cherubim of gold.
One cherub was at one end of the mercy seat, and another cherub was at the other end of the mercy seat.
They spread their wings over the mercy seat.
He made the table that stands before it of pure gold.
He cast four gold rings for it, two rings on each side, as holders by which they could grasp it when carrying it.
And he made carrying poles for the ark and the table and covered them with gold.
He made the table’s utensils of gold: dishes, bowls, cups, and vessels for pouring.
He made the lampstand that gives light of gold,
with a solid central shaft and branches at its sides.
Branches sprouted from its shaft, three on one side and three on the other, all alike.

Their lamps were on their tops. Its rounded ornaments and its holders were made from the same piece, so that lamps could rest on them. The lamp rests were above everything beneath them. It was solid and entirely of gold.
Its seven lamps upon it were of gold, and everything used to tend its lamps was of gold.
He also overlaid the pillars with silver and cast gold rings for its pillars. He overlaid its bars with gold, and he overlaid the pillars for the curtain with gold and made their hooks of gold.
He made the clasps of the tabernacle of gold, and the clasps of the courtyard and the clasps by which the curtain above was drawn of bronze.

He cast the capitals of the pillars of silver, and the capitals of the pillars for the entrance of the tabernacle and the gate of the courtyard of bronze. He also made silver hooks above the pillars, and he overlaid them with silver.
He made the stakes of the tabernacle and the stakes of the courtyard of bronze.
He made the bronze altar from the bronze censers of the men who had sinned with Korah’s company.
He made all the altar’s utensils of bronze: the [?], its fire pans, its bowls, and the implements for taking out the meat.

He made a latticework grating for the altar, reaching halfway up from below so that the fire could reach it. He placed four bronze rings on the altar’s four sides as holders for the poles with which they carried the altar.
He made the holy anointing oil, and he made the fragrant incense, pure, according to the perfumer’s craft.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who fasted at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony on the day it was erected.

He made that basin so that Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons could wash their hands and feet in it when they entered the tabernacle of testimony and when they approached the altar to serve. They washed in it as the Lord had commanded Moses.
All the gold used for the work of the sanctuary, the gold of the tithes they brought in, amounted to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

The silver offered by the men who were counted in the assembly amounted to one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels by weight: one drachma per person, half a shekel according to the sanctuary shekel.
Everyone who entered the census, from twenty years old and upward, amounted to six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
Those one hundred talents of silver were used to cast the capitals of the tabernacle’s pillars and the capitals of the pillars for the curtain.
One hundred talents for one hundred capitals; one talent for each capital.
They used the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels to make hooks for the pillars, and they covered their capitals with gold and adorned them.
The bronze from the offering amounted to four hundred and seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
And from it he made the bases for the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony.
And the bases around the tabernacle, the bases for the courtyard gate, the pegs of the tabernacle, and the pegs around the courtyard.
And the iron nails around the altar, all the altar’s utensils, and all the equipment of the tabernacle of testimony.
The Israelites did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the gold left over from the offering into utensils for service before the Lord.
They made the remaining scarlet cloth, dark-colored cloth, and blue cloth into garments for Aaron to serve in, so that he could serve in them in the sanctuary.
They brought his garments to Moses, along with the tabernacle, its utensils, its clasps, its pillars, and its bases;
The ark of the commandment and its carrying poles, and the altar and all its utensils;
The oil used for anointing, the incense used for burning incense, and the pure lampstand;
Its lamps, the lights with which they give light in it, and the lamp oil;
The table on which they arrange the bread, all its utensils, and the bread they arrange on it;
Aaron’s sacred garments and his sons’ priestly garments;
The courtyard hangings, its pillars and its bases, the curtain for the tabernacle entrance, and the curtain for the courtyard gate;

All the tabernacle’s utensils and all its equipment, the ram hides made into leather, the coverings made from [?] skins, the other coverings, the pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle of testimony.
The Israelites carried out all the work just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work that had been done. They had done it just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Moses blessed them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
On the first day of the first month, you shall set up the tabernacle of testimony.
You shall put the ark of the testimony in place and screen the ark with the curtain.
You shall bring in the table and arrange it as prescribed. You shall bring in the lampstand and arrange its lamps.
You shall place the golden incense altar, on which incense is burned, before the ark of the testimony, and put a curtain at the entrance of the tent of the testimony.
You shall place the altar on which sacrifices are offered toward the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and you shall set up the courtyard around it.
You shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything inside it. You shall consecrate it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.
You shall anoint the altar on which sacrifices are offered and all its utensils.
You shall consecrate the altar, and that altar shall be most holy.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony and wash them with water.
You shall dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, and he shall be a priest for me.
You shall also bring his sons and dress them in those garments.
You shall anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall be priests for me. This anointing shall establish their priesthood throughout their generations forever.
Moses did everything that the Lord commanded him; that is what he did.
In the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt, on the first day of the new moon, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle, put its capitals in place, inserted its bars, and erected its pillars.
He spread out the tabernacle's curtains and put the covering over the tabernacle, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He took the writings of the commandments and put them inside, and placed its carrying poles beside the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the screening curtain, and screened off the ark of the testimony, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the tabernacle of the testimony, on the north side of the tabernacle of the testimony, outside the tabernacle's curtain.
He arranged the bread of the offering on it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the tabernacle of the testimony, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He arranged its lamps before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the golden incense altar in the tent of the testimony, in front of the curtain.
He burned on it the incense he had prepared, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the altar on which sacrifices were offered at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony.
He set up the enclosure around the tabernacle and around the altar, and Moses finished all his work.
The cloud covered the tabernacle of the testimony, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the tabernacle of the testimony, because the cloud overshadowed it and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on their journeys.
But if the cloud did not lift, they would not set out until the day the cloud lifted.
For the cloud rested over the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of all Israel, wherever they traveled.
